what:
Derived-artifact resync design (Apr 21 2026, final). Problem: some settings produce on-disk files whose content depends on the setting (currently only .ignore from memories.hideFromGrep, extensible). Hook-read settings don't need resync because get_setting re-reads config.json fresh on every invocation.

Four trigger points, all calling the same `resyncDerivedArtifacts(projectRoot)` function in src/memory/init.ts:
1. `aide-memory config KEY VALUE` CLI write → config.ts applySideEffects → instant
2. MCP server startup (new Claude Code session OR /mcp reconnect) → autoUpdateIfNeeded calls it unconditionally before the version check
3. Any hook fire after direct edit of .aide/config.json (mid-session drift-repair) → mtime check in shared read-config.sh fires background resync when mtime differs from cached value (.aide/cache/config-mtime.txt)
4. Cross-session propagation: session A edits config → session B's next hook fire picks it up via the same mtime cache (shared file)

Multi-session semantics: each Claude Code session spawns its OWN MCP child process. No shared long-running daemon. Sessions don't coordinate. The shared file-mtime cache is the propagation channel. Each session's hooks independently detect drift via mtime.

The mtime check goes in read-config.sh (not per-hook) so every hook inherits the behavior without per-script changes.
why: User asked about multi-session behavior and whether mtime check should be on all hooks vs just detect-correction. Final design is simpler than initial proposal: centralize in read-config.sh so every hook gets it, and rely on shared cache file for cross-session propagation. Capturing so future implementation matches the agreed design.
